case.background: Monochromatic light passes through two narrow parallel slits and forms alternating bright and dark bands on a screen. Vary only the listed controls and infer a quantitative law for adjacent bright-fringe spacing.
initial_observations: Blocking either slit removes the regular band pattern.
Changing the geometry shifts the bright bands, but the dependence is not given.

controls.description: Wavelength of the monochromatic incident light.
controls.name: wavelength_nm

controls.description: Distance from the two slits to the observation screen.
controls.name: screen_distance_m

controls.description: Center-to-center separation of the two narrow slits.
controls.name: slit_separation_mm

instruments.description: A monochromatic source, two narrow parallel slits, a movable screen, and a scale for measuring adjacent bright fringes.
instruments.name: double_slit_screen

notes: The slits remain narrow and parallel, and the screen stays normal to the beam.

For objective final scoring, FinalSubmission.model must be 'expression'. FinalSubmission.parameters must equal {'outputs': {'fringe_spacing_mm': EXPR}}. EXPR is family-neutral arithmetic: a finite JSON number, {'var': CONTROL_NAME}, or {'op': OP, 'args': [EXPR, ...]}; OP is add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, negate, exp, or log. This track-wide grammar is shared across discovery cases; use only public control names. No candidate law family or parameter slots are supplied.

readouts.description: Mean separation between adjacent bright fringes.
readouts.name: fringe_spacing_mm

case.title: Discover the double-slit fringe response
